html:
The Mixtecs are an Indigenous people of southern Mexico, whose homeland, La Mixteca, covers western Oaxaca and parts of Puebla and Guerrero. They call themselves Ñuu Savi, "people of the rain". The map shows them in 800 and 900.

The Mixteca was never one empire. It was a land of many small kingdoms, each ruled by a lord from a hilltop town, linked by marriage and war. After the fall of Monte Albán, Mixtec power grew in the Valley of Oaxaca.

The Mixtecs were among the finest artists of Mesoamerica:

  • painted deerskin books, such as the Codex Zouche-Nuttall, which record the genealogies and wars of their lords;
  • the life of the warlord Eight Deer Jaguar Claw, who united much of the Mixteca in the eleventh century;
  • gold and turquoise work, such as the treasure found in Tomb 7 at Monte Albán.

The Aztecs conquered much of the Mixteca in the late 1400s, and the Spanish arrived in the 1520s. Mixtec is still spoken today by several hundred thousand people. See also the Mixtec states on the map in later years.
